sentences.text: First, what counts as a vessel?
Pretty much anything that floats and can carry people or things across the water: boats, ships, barges, hovercraft, even seaplanes and wing-in-ground craft.
A power-driven vessel is anything propelled by machinery.
A sailing vessel is under sail, with one important catch: any engine she has must not be in use.
So here’s a classic exam question.
A sailboat is heading out the pass with every sail up, and her engine is running to help her along.
The moment that engine turns the prop, the rules treat her like any other powerboat.
And a seaplane is simply an aircraft designed to maneuver on the water.
